Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (To three songbirds) Look at that, my fine feathered friends! (He mounts his handiwork onto the tree trunk) Not a bad bit of work, even if I do say so myself. Just wait till you see the hidden surprise. (He pushes a red button on the front of the bird house, which bears the words 'home tweet home'. Its walls spring outward, revealing various miniature items including a fountain and a spiral staircase) Oh, nothing? Not even a sausage? No matter. (He pushes the button once again and the birdhouse folds back to its normal state) Wait until Linda and the kids see it. It'll blow their tiny minds. Well, not their tiny minds, that's not fair.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Guys, come and look at this. This is an actual replica of an artist's interpretation of what some random guy of no significance believed that the chariot of Asparagus might have looked like. And this is Asparagus, the greatest warrior in all of Greece. With this golden chariot, he would win every race. And here he is defeating the Minotaur, a creature that's half-man, half-bull. Asparagus defeated him using the head of Medusa, a creature so ugly she could turn people to stone with just one look.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, so many things, really. Music, hobbies, you kids. Ooh! You know what she really likes, is my famous rhubarb creme brulee. I used to make it for her all the time when we were dating. Oh, it made her so happy. (Candace leaves but Lawrence doesn't notice her leaving.) You know, I should get out my toque and blowtorch and make one for her today. What a good idea, Candace. Thank you. (notices Candace has left) Candace? Well, all right then.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (reading) "Thank you for coming here today to hear my speech on the history of the ancient Ornithorhynchan tribe. (At this point, Candace's eyes begin to become heavy and she tries in vain to stay awake.) The Ornithorhynchans were a platypus-worshipping society known for painting themselves teal-blue and wearing elaborate platypus-themed costumes for their various dances and rituals."

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, actually there is one thing you probably won't be able to find here. An 1807 Dorcham and Wesley Boot Scraper, only one of them was ever made, (dramatically) and it's been lost to the mists of time! Oh, if only I could find that, I'd be the envy of the entire antiquing community; especially Worthington Dubois, (he clenches his fists) my antiquing nemesis!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, this? It's an escape chamber from an old vaudeville show. In the old days, men would go into these things and pretend to be locked inside and then they would "escape" to the amazement of the crowd. Here, let me show you. (goes inside the chamber) You see? All you need to do is just... (tries to escape) Uh.... Hmm...

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (On screen) Oh, the kids are going to love this Austrian-style cuckoo clock. Oh, I wish you'd let me buy the large one. (The Melt-inator fires, melting the tires of the car and making Linda scream) Maybe we should pull over and see what's going on. (cut to them examining the flatness) That's peculiar.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, the ship held together pretty good, didn't it? (Cut to reveal Lawrence is holding the wheel surrounded by debris from the wreckage.) Of course, we'll have to re-attach the wheel (Cut to reveal the sloop on a rock.) and fix that, uh, giant hole. Now, kids, are you all right?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Gather 'round kids, and I'll tell you a story about the close-encounter. It was a dark night, and I was out for a drive, when my motorcar began to behave strangely. Twas then when a bright green light started shining and I couldn't help but walking towards the light scource.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, yes and I'm British, and so you think I'm supposed to like bird watching. (Imitating a British accent) Oh, I'm British, so I'll in the conservatory with tea and a crumpet. I'm saying that ironically but actually that sounds quite good. So I'm going to do that. Ta.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (inspecting the hole) Whoa, this doesn't look too good at all. Kids, don't come up here! It's far too dangerous! Mum and I will fix the boat. Candace, why don't you look for some food? And, boys, you could find us some shelter if you like. We may be here for a while.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Linda! I don't know what's come over me, but I'm starting to get the most wild and uninhibited ideas! You know how every day for the last twenty years I've relaxed with a nice cup of Earl Grey? Well, not today, Linda! Today, I'm putting out all the stops! Darjeeling!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, that's the question isn't it. Only one of these can be the true Dorcham and Westley. And no doubt a wrong choice will trigger a nasty booby trap. Boot scrapers were famously vengeful people. This could take every ounce of antiquing knowledge that I possess.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ooh, you know, kids, this theater was built over 70 years ago in this Neo-Egyptian style. And apparently, there used to be a pharaoh's tomb display with a mummy in a sarcophagus. I mean, you couldn't pick a better place to watch a classic, old mummy movie.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, let's have a look then. Oh, yes. I've seen this before. It's a commemorative coin from the nineteen hundred and three Danville World's Fair. Many steam-driven devices were introduced to the world back then. It must have been quite an event...

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And here's the 17th century Whiskershire spring stick, which belonged to the Earl of Whiskershire. (A man dressed in royal garments and a mouse costume appears on screen. Lawrence's phone rings.) Oh, 'scuse me for a second. Hullo.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, your mother's jazz trio has a gig at the Mayor's Day festivities, and I shall be running the antiques auction, oh yes! I'm very excited because we have a collection of steamrollers on the block, all imported from England.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: OK, now let's see. "Lead the way for the lovely lady with an elegant wave of your hand. "For you and only you, insert your name here..." Oh, thanks for the light. Hey! No, no, wait! No, no, help me put it out! Do something!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, Candace there's no such thing as lots of things, and there's such thing as many other things. (Spins the steering wheel) Is Nosey such a thing? (The car stops turning) Well, you see, that's the thing, isn't it?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, I did. Yes, of course I did, although she doesn't really care about this stuff. Anyway, they're practically giving 'em away online! D'you know, it's even better than the Oklahoma land rush of 1889!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, it's hard to explain actually, taking the flip pass from the winner, shoulder deking the defense men, and then, tossing it right over the old glove hand. Oh, it just takes hold of you like a fever!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, your mother's going to meet a lot of exciting and cool people. What if I'm…I'm no longer cool enough for your mum? I'm hardly a rock star, am I? (walking away sadly) I"m afraid I'm hopelessly nerdy.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh yeah, brilliant. But I better check with Mom about this. (At phone) Uh, hello honey, yes, yes, oh gosh, I love you too, darling. Uh, are you aware the boys have a monster truck in the backyard?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Chuckles) Well... (Dashes off and comes back wearing fishing gear) If I must. (Camera zooms into him) Well, who knows? I might even be persuaded to tell a few of my world-famous fishing stories.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ooo, those crazy coots! I'll just do an old-school drop de-turn on them, eh? Cut back up on the face, through the sloop, do a nice inner tail, and drop into the green room for a bit of tune time.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I said, "John, it's great, I love the tune but the words. 'All you need is a Phillips head screwdriver', it just doesn't really ring true, does it?" (Phineas and Ferb reappear on the boat.)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, yes, you have fun at the castle party tonight. (putting the mask on his head) If you need anything, your mother and I will be here scaring the sugar out of the little trick or treaters.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yeah, mom and I are getting rid of a few old things at the antique store, but I think I've got just what you need. (a moment later...) A snow cone machine just like when I was a kid!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Is it really? (pauses) How remarkable. Well, we're the Flynn-Fletcher family. Two adults, three children, (holding up a pet carrier with Perry inside it) and our pet platypus, Perry.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: It's the new, digitally remastered third series of Pinhead Pierre! (boys bounce down on a large inflatable ball) Only the best series ever and my most favorite show ever. That's all.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (sighs) That didn't go over as well as I'd hoped. Mmmm, perhaps I need to spuh-ruce it up more! Sprrrrrruce! Sprrrrrrrrrrrrrr—Ahh! Ooh! Ow! I do believe I've sprrrrrrrained my elbow.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh! My word, there's a truck-driving pharmacist and he's pressing his face up against his windshield. Oh, that's what I love about you Americans. You-You're like big, fun children.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, that's not very nice, is it. But look on the bright side, Candace, this year we might take home one just like this. Ta da! (Makes a W with his three fingers on his forehead)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (He examines the scroll) A Dorcham and Westley Boot Scraper's map! But only three of them were ever made, (dramatically) and they were lost to the mists of- oh I'm doing it again.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (He gasps) By Harry! That's Boot Scrape! The secret language of the ancient boot scapers. (Reading) To gain the world, and halt the wintle, reverse your mind, and mind the lintel.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: What? Everyone knows that boy would rather be somewhere else. What about you two? The crops are so far ahead, would you like to spend the rest of the summer at swim camp on Naboo?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well the map has led us to Boot Scrapers Hall. (They enter Boot Scrapers Hall) Oh, the spirit of Danville, see how his sole gleams, the Boot Scapers took their craft seriously.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: It's such a waste to get rid of them. See? Look. Chopsticks and Ponzu sauce. That's Japanese but-but look, there's also a Chinese fortune cookie, that's what's known as fusion.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Right-o! (runs to get it) It's been at my bedside all these years! (pushes coffee table over) Hop on, boys! (all sit on rug) We're about to take off on the ride of a lifetime!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, I'll decide where we go on vacation as soon as I clean out Perry's litter box. (looks into the litter box with the Hawaiian islands drawn on it) Hey, how about Hawaii?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And here, we have a marvel 16th century wardrobe. We have one just like this when I was a schoolboy. And inside it was another land filled with magical woodland creatures.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, that was the best Father's Day flight yet! It brought back some some wonderful old memories and created a lot of new ones. Thank you, boys, for making this possible!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well here we are gang, the semi-annual Tri-State Area antique show and swap meet. Here you can find anything under the sun, literally, because it's held outdoors. Ha, ha.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh! That was close. (rights the car back up) Whoops! Dropped my address. (picks up the paper) Well, (places paper on the sun visor) 6106, Palindrome Road, here I come!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (to Linda) Oh, and another little tidbit about the ancient Egyptians (Doofenshmirtz and Perry run past them in the background) is that both men and women wore makeup.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, you'd be surprised, what with Steamroller Today magazine and Wacky Steamroller videos posted on the Internet. The public is going crazy for the flattening arts.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, excellent. It's good to see you boys taking an interest in Greek mythology. I'm doing the same. I've got over 12 hours of gladiator movies here I wanna watch.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, there you are. (to Ignatius) Um, I'd like you to me my wife Linda, and our kids and their friends. Everyone, this is Ignatius Ukareamü, my old college chum.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And that is why the 18th century sewing thimble was not only a slice of history, but a compelling example of American grit and perseverance. Hmm? Hmm? Hmm? Yes?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Look at this. I got a traffic ticket from that camera they installed across the street. Oh, that blasted device picks up everything on the block 24 hours a day.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (As he stops blowing into the pipe attached to the salad bowl on Linda's head, revealing him as the source of the whirring noise) Was that Candace on the phone?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hello, girls. (Wide shot to reveal the "rain" is actually the sprinkler.) Don't mind me. I'm just givin' the lawn a bit of a drink. (turns it off) It's off now.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, look. This T-Rex footprint was found not 30 yards from this very spot. Hey, it says here that this fossil was dug up right near our very own neighborhood.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Soon, the entire village of Whiskershire began following the Earl's lead to, of course... (phone rings again) Uh, do forgive me. I-I-I'm awfully sorry. Hello?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, we couldn't very well serve that cake, the way those wild penguins tore it apart, could we? And to think that they were carried away by a freak tornado!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Look, boys; it's your cousins visiting from England! They're here to see the exhibition football match between Danville and their beloved Snifferton Nostrils.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, go on. Play track three! It's the one where a group of truckers take down a corrupt police force using only their trucks and their saucy colloquialisms.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yes, the Boot Scrapers were renowned for their elaborate spiral staircases. If that Dorcham and Westley Boot Scraper still exists, we'll find it down here.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hmmm, visual aids. Ah, that's how I can (rolling his r's) sprruce it up a little. Sprrrruce! Sprrrrrruce! Spuuuuuuuuh-ruce! Ha ha ha, ah, very good then.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Say, there is something pretty peculiar going on here, now, don't tell me! You turned the entire garage upside-down, now why on earth would you do that?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Uh, L-Linda, my dear, I love you, but you couldn't have chosen a worse moment to go completely bonkers! I'm sorry, but I've got to call you back! Bye!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hmm... and this leads directly to the 1960's. (unplugs the jukebox) Oh, well, time to get this beaut to the antique shop. (wheels it away) Ta, boys!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh dear, the poor thing. Look at that. Wait a minute. Antidisestablishmentarianism? That's more of an ideological stance than a disease. Isn't it?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Boys, I've got some good news for you. I've arranged for you to play a little exhibition match between the periods of the Danville Ice Trays game.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ooh! Merry old England. How I love our yearly holiday to my parents' home. Big Ben, Buckingham Palace, oh, the White Cliffs of Dover. Stonehenge.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Wish me luck, boys. (at the mechanical mother) Hello, old dear, so lovely to see you. (bows) I've brought you some peonies. (pulls out a bouquet)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Alright, I want to see everyone out there on the dance floor. Parents, kids, giant robots, sure why not? Let's kick this party into second gear!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: This statue, which stands outside the Whiskershire Rectory, still holds the Earl's actual spring stick, yes. The spring stick is used as such

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: The Cavern of Secrets. This entire room was made from materials scraped off the boots of Danville Elders, who were highly creative engineers.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I thought so. Yes, easy-peasy, that one. Next, the tip of the shoelace. Yes, yes, that little hard tip at the end of a shoelace is... Honey?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (opening the box) Oh, my! An exact replica of Father's biplane! Oh, it's perfect! (giving his daughter a hug) Thank you so much, sweetheart!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Thank you for coming here today to hear my speech on the ancient Ornithorhynchan tribe. The Ornithorhynchans were a platypus-worshipping...

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Reading from a newspaper inside a taxicab driving past the fight)) Good heavens, look at that! They're making a new version of Jane Eyre.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, it's not actually called a boat, darling, it's called a sloop. When we're on sea there's no right or left, only port and starboard.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Do you know, Candace, I don't remember much of what happened here today, (hugs his daughter) but I'll never forget this moment with you.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, hold your horses, kids. It says here that the lead of Cirque de Lune has a severe allergy. They're canceling today's performance.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I can do that? Hey, I don't remember seeing this part. Hmm, (Laughs) well, it looks just like Candace. Hey, honey, you gotta see this!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, I am a little rusty on my Hawaiian, but here goes. Buenos dias, señor. Me llamo Lawrence. (Good day, sir. My name is Lawrence.)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (leads them into the garage) Oh, yes. It's the same car I had when I was a lad. I figured it would be ready when you were old enough.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yes, it does look that way, doesn't it? (the ball comes back down, he continues playing Keepy-Uppy) However, looks can be deceiving.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Why do I get the feeling I wasn't supposed to see that? (trips on a cable) Ooh! That hurt. (lands in the memory eraser and mumbles)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Chuckles) That was the best! And I happen to own the single greatest collection of Pinhead Pierre paraphernalia in all the world.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Walks in) Oh, hello, boys! Are we having a party, Baljeet? And Baljeet and. . . wait a moment, if he's Baljeet you must be. . . ?

Name: Lawrence (2nd Dimension)
Dialog: Boys, what are you doing here? You'd better get inside before the Doofbot catches you. I'm off to the factory. See you next week!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, rapture! This is my favorite part of the Danville Harbor Day's festival! The annual shark reenactment. Let's checketh it out.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, just a few vocal exercises before my big speech for the committee of the Danville Museum. Would you like a little sneak peek?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, boys, we're off to the Center for Historically Relevant Botanical Gardens, a virtual treasure trove of topical topiaries.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, I can't believe it! It seems my video traffic ticket's been cleared. I guess there is someone up there looking out for me.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, what a phenomenal finale to our finale. Congratulations and cued us to our two winners. And there wasn't even a contest.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And now, ladies and gentlemen, what you've all been waiting to bid on. I give you, the antique steamrollers! (crowd cheers)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: No dear, the bird took a left at Snores-ville, and is up here in Danville. Can I get up high? (Candace high-fives Lawrence)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: See, Candace? Even a trained professional has trouble from time to time. Now, I want you to just relax, and park this car!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: ...So he said, "Try ignoring it and hope it goes away. (Camera zooms into them) And you know what? It did. After 17 weeks.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hello. we had the most amazing time. Look! I found this 19th century barometer. Anything interesting happen 'round here?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, well, be sure to be home in time for the barbecue. We're gonna be watching Kermillian's Comet fly past the Earth.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Such beauty, such tranquility. A fisherman's paradise. Yes, of all the lakes in the world, I'm glad we picked the Nose.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (notices the lair entrance) How peculiar. Anybody there -- (falls through the door and slides down to Perry's lair) Oh.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (he rolls his tongue) Hello, hello hello! Can you guess what my DJ costume is for tonight's big Mardi Gras block party?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Why yes, yes it is! Jeremy, you have your license, don't you? You can take Candace for a ride in it when it's finished.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (voice over) I bought us tickets to their farewell concert. Oh, we were a handsome, stylish couple back in those days.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (on CB radio) Yes, yes, this is Cheeky Monkey. You're shaking the windows. What's your handle, good buddy? Come back.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, seeing as the place is falling apart anyway. (He grabs all the remaining boot scrapers, and the three run out)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (yelling to Linda) Dear! Are you aware the boys have turned the garage upside-down, looking for Ferb's skateboard?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, it took three hours for them to untangle my hair from the gears, but I never lost my grip on that lava lamp.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Kermillian's Comet was named after an ancient Danville astronomer, Augustus Kermillian, who discovered the comet.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (comes up) So, what are we looking at? (pause, Candace and Linda look at him) Oh. Oh, right, haha! (goes back in)

Name: Lawrence-2
Dialog: Well, I don't suppose there's any reason to hide this stuff anymore. So, yes! As they used to say, "Have a ball!"

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, kids. I'll leave you in charge of the machine and be easy on your sister. She's been a bit on edge lately.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (walks in, boys are sitting on rug looking at TV with controllers) Well, another interior design crisis averted.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (at a smug Doofenshmirtz) I don't know how you did it! I don't even think I understood the event, but good show!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Then it must be...the day I realized how cute you are when you're angry? (Phineas and Ferb stare at each other)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, I think it's rather sweet that Betty Jo and Grandpa Clyde invite you kids and all your friends every year.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay. (on CB radio) Uh, breaker, breaker, 1-9. This is Cheeky Monkey. Anybody got their flappers on out there?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, as it turns out, it was just a tow truck driver I had called. He charged up my battery, and off he went!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, dear, it looks like everyone's found something to do, and Chez Afrique dinner reservation's in an hour.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And just to express how sorry we are, here's my credit card. You have our permission to ruin us financially.

Name: Lawrence/Max
Dialog: You know, I feel strangely comfortable like this. But how can I be a rock star if nobody's ever heard of me?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yes, but fat lot of good it did me. I mean here we are, thirty years later and they've lost our reservation.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, hi honey, we were just listening to some records. It's what we used to use for music when we were kids.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (carrying pillows) Oh, that's wonderful, honey. Not a single day goes by when I don't appreciate my PHD.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I say, boys, you can barely feel the road! It corners like a dream! Pinhead Pierre, eat your heart out!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Speaking of coins... What's this here? Behind your ear? (Reaches behind Phineas's ear.) It's a quarter!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hey, you know, kids, these fossils are of creatures that lived here in Danville millions of years ago.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (pauses video) You see, right there. Modern cartoon shows never ask the really big questions, do they?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, honey, but don't press the red button on it, will you? I want to be there when you see it, okay?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: ...and their kids, Beckham, Beckham, Pele, Beckham, Pele, and Eliza. Well, her middle name is Beckham.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ah, my university chummy has been trying to get us to visit his animal research station for years now.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, Candace. All you have to do is park between this plastic trash can, and that plastic trash can.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, uh, let's move on, shall we? This exhibit is kindly Old Man Simmons—Hey! Who's up for milkshakes?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Uh, okay. (Drives right into a cornfield.) This seems to have a little more corn than most shortcuts.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, yes, we're ready for our journey of self-discovery while crawling through the belly of the Earth.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (while tying his tie) So it goes over, under, around and through. Ooh, lovely. Time to open the shop.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, well, so much for that. I guess it's not a total loss. I mean, this is still presentable, right?

Name: Lawrence Robot
Dialog: Jolly good, Candace. As long as it's okay with Mum, it's okay with me. Stiff upper lip and all that.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (oblivious to what's going on) I thought I was already confirmed. Prepared my speech and everything.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, you can say what you like about Candace, but there's nothing primitive about her imagination.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, right-o. (to Phineas) Ooh, just a minute, does that skateboard have a Union Jack on the bottom?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (as he walks back) Remember to keep that foot elevated. (to the other two) What a lovely, old girl.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I'll be right there, sweetheart, I'm just clearing a spot for the trophy we're going to win today.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Bubble gum, bubble gum, running in a sack. (Candace smiles) Hop to the finish and don't look back!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hello, boys, splendid job on the hockey rink. (He crashes into a snowbank) Well, that was amusing.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And we'll love them anyway. Candace, the sooner we get started, the sooner we all get to go home.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Under his breath) Got it. (At Adrian) Oh, hey, Ady, how about one last little event? Keepy-Uppy?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: That's why our couch cushions are worn so unevenly. 'Cause we're always on the edge of our seats.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh no Buford, they were real. They were tiny rooms where you could talk on the phone in private.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Look, I'm telling you, it's the most peculiar thing I've ever seen. It looks just like Candace.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ahem. Look, darling, I'm in the middle of something right here, so I'll have to phone you back.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Driving) I'm sorry, boys, but we only have 'til sundown to return this RV to the rental place.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (voice breaking in tears) Thank you so much, boys! I can't think of a better Father's Day gift!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (referring to the birdhouse) Oh, yes, of course I do, honey. I made it myself. Do you like it?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (from inside the tank) Uh, dear, as long as you're getting up, could you get me some more pie?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And that is why we celebrate Harbor Day every year with a reenactment. Here cometh the shark.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hidden deep in the bowels of the pyramids. (Phone rings) Whoops, better put this on vibrate.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (unpauses video) Oh, well, at least Perry will watch these with me. Won't you, Perry? Perry?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: It was either back up the fire escape or lose the pants altogether. Then suddenly it hit me.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, let me see... He had some kind of a German accent, and ooh, he was wearing a lab coat.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Why does everyone guess that? No, I'm a Mardi Gras jester. Speaking of which, where's Perry?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And Lot Number 2 is a little beaut from Aveling & Porter built in 1924. Do I have any bids?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (voice over) I'd never so much as held your mother's hand, but that night, I made my move.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: All right, then. I'll clear all these drawers and boxes out later, darling. See you, boys!

Name: Lawrence

Dialog: Well, I'm sure you'll hear plenty more fantastical stories during Gran and Gramp's visit.

Dialog: Yes, indeed. Often you had to negotiate many booby traps that were set centuries before.

Dialog: I did, didn't I? Well, I suppose I get melodramatic when I start talking about antiques.
